Add a nested-set upstream index to a hydrofabric GeoPackage

Source: R/add_upstream_index.R
add_upstream_index.Rd

Stamps upstream_id (depth-first pre-order ordinal from each outlet) and num_upstreams (strict upstream count) on the flowpaths, flowlines, divides, and network layers, so the flowpaths upstream of X are those with upstream_id in (upstream_id[X], upstream_id[X] + num_upstreams[X]], an O(1) range filter instead of a traversal.

Usage

add_upstream_index(
  ngen_gpkg,
  flowpaths_layer = "flowpaths",
  nexus_layer = "nexus",
  propagate_to = c("flowlines", "divides", "network")
)

Arguments

ngen_gpkg

Path to the NextGen GeoPackage.

flowpaths_layer

Flowpath layer name. Default "flowpaths".

nexus_layer

Nexus layer name. Default "nexus".

propagate_to

Layers to stamp by flowpath_id. Default c("flowlines", "divides", "network").

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of flowpath_id, upstream_id, and num_upstreams. Adds those integer columns to the layers in place.

Details

The values are specific to this file's network (a per-VPU, merged, or subset gpkg each gets a correct-scope index) and are not a persistent key. The compute (fp -> nexus -> fp resolution + nested set) is hfutils::hf_upstream_index(); reads and writes are attribute-only via DBI, so it is safe at merged/national scale.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
add_upstream_index("ngen_vpu01.gpkg")
# flowpaths strictly upstream of fp-8:
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "ngen_vpu01.gpkg")
anchor <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT upstream_id u, num_upstreams n
                           FROM flowpaths WHERE flowpath_id = '8'")
dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT flowpath_id FROM flowpaths WHERE upstream_id > %d AND upstream_id <= %d",
  anchor$u, anchor$u + anchor$n))
} # }
